articles.title: F1 Azerbaijan GP: George Russell takes dominant pole as Kimi Antonelli crashes out
articles.summary: George Russell takes his fifth pole of 2026 at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix while championship leader Kimi Antonelli won't start higher than 16th after...
articles.body:
Mercedes driver George Russell has beaten Charles Leclerc to take a dominant pole at F1's Azerbaijan GP, while team-mate and title favourite Kimi Antonelli crashed out of Q1.

At the 6km Baku City Circuit, Antonelli tagged the barriers on the inside of the Turn 1 left-hander during Q1, unable to limp back home in his Mercedes W17 with terminal front-left suspension damage. Antonelli had already set a time quick enough to advance to Q2, but was out of the session and is set to start 16th at best.

Team-mate Russell, who had already proven his rapid pace through Thursday's practice sessions, capitalised fully to take a dominant pole ahead of Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri, the Briton's fifth pole of the campaign.

McLaren sprung an early surprise in Q3 when Piastri and Lando Norris jumped early pacesetter Russell to top the first barrage of qualifying runs. Off the back of a messy brace of practices, the papaya squad had yet to string together optimal qualifying laps, with Norris even suspecting something was wrong in his car in Q1.

But Piastri's 1m43.571s lap proved an achievable target for Russell to beat, with the Briton going half a second faster on his second run to set a rapid 1m43.037s, which none of his competitors could find an answer for.

On the final run, Russell took yet another five-tenth chunk out of his own benchmark to set a dominant 1m42.526s pole lap.

Ferrari employed a different run plan by delaying its first run, which yielded Leclerc provisional second, and the Monegasque found another tenth that secured that position on the grid ahead of Piastri, albeit a sobering eight tenths behind Russell.

Isack Hadjar celebrated his return from injury with fourth on the grid, while Norris slipped up on his final attempt and settled for fifth ahead of Hamilton. Pierre Gasly secured seventh for Alpine as Max Verstappen could only manage eighth following a suspected energy deployment issue, and lost further time under a yellow flag caused by Norris.

Carlos Sainz made full use of Williams' upgraded FW48 to claim ninth, as Franco Colapinto qualified tenths following an erratic Q3 session.

Russell topped Q2 with a late 1m43.462s effort, two tenths ahead of Verstappen as it promised to set up a tight pole shoot-out.

The battle for the final Q3 spots was as close as it has been all season with Williams now in the hunt, and Sainz capitalised to go ninth and claim a rare Q3 berth. The dramatic rate of track evolution meant drivers were fueled up for multiple laps to try and peak on their final run In the dying seconds Alpine's Colapinto snatched 10th away from Haas driver Oliver Bearman, joining his team-mate Gasly in the next segment.

Racing Bulls was the biggest victim in Q2 with Liam Lawson out in 12th, followed by the second Williams of Alex Albon and Esteban Ocon in the remaining Haas. Arvid Lindblad could only muster 15th to continue what has been a messy weekend so far for the Briton, off the back of an FP2 crash which team principal Alan Permane ascribed to "rookie enthusiasm".

Russell also led the way in Q1 after Antonelli disappeared, demoting Verstappen at the end of the session with a 1m43.615s lap. In the background, Williams comfortably made it through with both of its upgraded cars.

On a high-speed track exposing its power unit deficit, Audi paid the price of Williams' progress as Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg were both eliminated in 17th and 18th. The four cars from Cadillac and Aston Martin were also punched out, with Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll already facing a back-of-the-grid penalty for Honda power unit changes.

articles.title: Asian Games: India win six medals, including shooting gold, as Baranica makes pole vault history
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a six-medal haul on a packed Friday at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, highlighted by a historic bronze for Baranica
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a six-medal haul on a packed Friday at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, highlighted by a historic bronze for Baranica Elangovan in women’s pole vault and a shooting gold from Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet. The day also brought silver medals for Gulveer Singh in the men’s 10,000m and India’s men’s 50m rifle 3-position team, besides bronze medals in women’s shot put and table tennis mixed doubles.Baranica’s achievement was the landmark moment, as she became the first Indian athlete to win an Asian Games medal in pole vault, across both the men’s and women’s events.The six medals took India’s tally to 23 — two gold, nine silver and 12 bronze.Shooting finally strikes goldSuruchi and Kamaljeet ended India’s wait for a shooting gold by dominating the 10m air pistol mixed team final.The Indian pair combined for 484.6, with Suruchi contributing 245.7 and Kamaljeet 238.9. Their total was a Games and Asian record as they led from start to finish.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleThe gold provided a boost to India’s shooting campaign after the contingent had endured disappointment in several 10m events earlier in the competition.India also secured silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3-position team event through Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudrankksh Patil and Niraj Kumar. Their aggregate of 1762 left them four points behind China, who finished on 1766.Aishwary and Niraj also reached the individual final, finishing fifth and eighth respectively.Baranica makes pole vault historyBaranica cleared 4.15m to finish joint third in the women’s pole vault final. Kazakhstan’s Polina Ivanova also cleared 4.15m, and the two athletes were level on attempts before both failed to clear 4.25m.With neither able to improve on 4.15m and both tied on the countback, Baranica and Ivanova shared the bronze medal.The result marked a first for Indian athletics at the Asian Games, with Baranica becoming the country’s first medallist in pole vault.Compatriot Sindhusree Ganesha, meanwhile, finished without a valid mark. She failed to clear 3.85m in two attempts before also missing at 4m.Gulveer improves to silverLong-distance runner Gulveer Singh added another athletics medal, upgrading the bronze he won in the men’s 10,000m at the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou to silver.The 28-year-old clocked 28:29.38 to finish behind Bahrain’s Birhanu Balew, who produced a late surge to win gold in 28:27.51. Balew’s compatriot Albert Kiptoo took bronze in 28:34.38.A Naib Subedar in the Indian Army, Gulveer stayed with the leading pack for much of the race and remained in medal contention deep into the final stages before Balew pulled clear.Gulveer has also been in strong form in recent years, winning gold in both the 5,000m and 10,000m at the 2025 Asian Athletics Championships. At the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, he became the first Indian to win two track medals at a single edition, taking silver in the 10,000m and bronze in the 5,000m.Manpreet adds shot put bronzeIndia’s other athletics bronze came from Manpreet Kaur in the women’s shot put final.Manpreet produced a best throw of 17.17m to finish third, while compatriot Krishna Jayasankar Menon was fifth with 16.57m.China’s Jiayoan Song won gold with 19.40m, while Linru Zhang took silver with 18.14m.Badminton setback, squash and kabaddi boostThe day was not without disappointment for India. Defending badminton champions Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty suffered a first-round exit, losing 21-12, 19-21, 14-21 to Thailand’s Pakkapon Teeraratsakul and Peeratchai Sukphun.“It’s the mental part. Whenever we are mentally free, I think no one can beat us. But when we are stuck anywhere, we give opponents a chance to beat us,” Satwik said after the defeat.There was better news elsewhere. India’s men’s and women’s kabaddi sides stormed into their respective finals, keeping two more gold medals within reach.In squash, India assured themselves of three medals. Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar entered the mixed doubles semifinals, while Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh advanced to the last four in women’s and men’s singles respectively.Anahat defeated compatriot Tanvi Khanna 11-2, 11-5, 11-3, while Abhay beat Japan’s Ryonosuke Tsukue 11-4, 11-3, 11-6.India also secured a bronze in table tennis mixed doubles through Manush Shah and Diya Chitale, who lost their semifinal to China’s Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha.The women’s hockey side continued its unbeaten run with a 3-1 win over hosts Japan, while boxers Sachin Siwach advanced to the men’s 60kg quarterfinals. In athletics, India also secured places in the women’s 400m final through Kiran and Prachi, while Vishal TK advanced to the men’s 400m final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ruiloba y su Lancia encabezan un Rally de Llanes muy reñido
articles.standfirst: Cinco pilotos en sólo nueve segundos después de la primera etapa
articles.summary: Cinco pilotos en sólo nueve segundos después de la primera etapa
articles.body: El cronómetro se ha movido incesantemente a lo largo de la primera jornada de un Rally de Llanes que está resultando el más disputado en lo que va de curso. El ritmo ha sido frenético ya desde la ‘qualy’ de esta mañana, que ha encabezado ‘Cohete’ por apenas dos décimas. Después, en los tramos de la tarde, las diferencias han vuelto a ser mínimas hasta la súperespecial nocturna, que ha encumbrado a Diego Ruiloba como nuevo líder. El vencedor del 2024 está poniendo todo de su parte para hacerse otra vez con los honores en casa de su copiloto, Ángel Vela, sentado ahora ya al volante de su Lancia. Un segundo y medio constituye la exigua ventaja con la que partirá el asturiano mañana a los ocho tramos de la segunda jornada, remozada casi por completo en pos de refrescar una prueba con tanta tradición como esta. Iván Ares también está cuajando un regreso muy positivo a las carreteras del oriente asturiano, donde Efrén Llarena se ha hecho notar nada más reincorporarse al SuperCER, tomando la delantera al resto desde el principio, hasta que un problema de frenos le ha apartado del liderato. El jefe de filas de Skoda está sabiendo medir muy bien sus fuerzas en la cita que puede zanjar su cuarta corona. Además del tramo clasificatorio, el líder del SuperCER se ha ido a dormir con dos ‘scratch’ que le dejan cuarto, justo a espaldas del terceto de cabeza. Pepe López va poniendo todo de su parte en una cita especial para él, donde está volviendo a brillar sobre asfalto con el Hyundai. El madrileño es quinto, a 9 segundos del primer puesto, y mañana aún puede tener mucho que decir. Álvaro Muñiz marcha a continuación, seguido por Jorge Cagiao, que se ha encontrado enseguida más desenvuelto de lo que él mismo esperaba en sus primera experiencia en este terreno pilotando el nuevo Lancia del Recalvi Team. 1º- Diego Ruiloba / Ángel Vela (Lancia Ypsilon Rally2 HF Integrale), 35:09.7 2º- Iván Ares / Borja Rozada (Toyota GR Yaris Rally2), a 1.5 3º- Efrén Llarena / Sara Fernández (Toyota GR Yaris Rally2), a 2.0 4º- José Antonio Suárez / Alberto Iglesias (Skoda Fabia RS Rally2), a 8.3 5º- Pepe López / David Vázquez (Hyundai i20N Rally2), a 9.0

articles.title: Como criação de Brasília impacta mobilidade em meio à crise climática | G1
articles.standfirst: Eventos climáticos cada vez mais extremos paralisam grandes cidades, incluindo a capital. Especialistas discutem como crescimento do DF pode realçar episódios extremos do clima.
articles.summary: Eventos climáticos cada vez mais extremos paralisam grandes cidades, incluindo a capital federal. Especialistas discutem como crescimento do DF pode realçar episódios extremos do c
articles.body:
Ao longo dos anos, eventos climáticos – cada vez mais extremos – se tornaram capazes de paralisar grandes centros urbanos. O direito de ir e vir é um desafio urbano que mobiliza especialistas e altera as rotinas de milhares de pessoas em todo o mundo . No Distrito Federal, não é diferente.

Na primeira em uma série de três reportagens, o g1 mostra, com o auxílio de especialistas, como a construção e o crescimento da capital impactam na mobilidade urbana e são capazes de realçar episódios extremos do clima.

➡️Nos próximos dias, o g1 mostra também como esses impactos já são sentidos atualmente – e o que é preciso fazer para reverter esse quadro.

Engarrafamento no Eixão Sul, em Brasília — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Monumentalidade, concreto, formas geométricas e curvas . Brasília foi fundada na década de 1960, no meio do Planalto Central, e logo se tornou um dos mais expressivos símbolos da arquitetura moderna em todo mundo.

O modernismo surgiu, entre as décadas de 1930 e 1940, da necessidade de dar conforto às populações que viviam em cidades inchadas pela Revolução Industrial.

Segundo o presidente do Conselho de Arquitetura e Urbanismo (CAU) do DF, Ricardo Meira, o plano original do arquiteto Lúcio Costa valorizava a " caminhabilidade" .

"Ele pensou na lógica em que as pessoas, a uma distância máxima de 500 m da sua casa, tivessem tudo o que precisassem, inclusive lazer, educação, igreja, comércio."

Longos trechos viários: as vias urbanas do DF na década de 1960 e 1970

A ideia vale para o Plano Piloto, mas não se expandiu com o crescimento populacional e o surgimento das regiões administrativas , explica a professora da Universidade de Brasília ( UnB ) e doutora em arquitetura Liza Andrade.

"As cidades satélites não foram completamente urbanizadas, com desenvolvimento econômico suficiente, o que cria ainda dependência do Plano Piloto. Brasília é muito espalhada. Isso tudo é difícil para a mobilidade urbana", afirma.

A especialista destaca o conceito de monofuncionalidade , também ligada ao modernismo – ou seja, a ideia de criar setores específicos para moradia, trabalho, lazer .

A partir daí, nasce também a necessidade de que a grande maioria da população se desloque com mais frequência para cumprir as tarefas diárias . Onde se mora, quase não se trabalha e quase não se diverte.

"Brasília foi planejada para abrigar uma população estimada de 500 mil habitantes. O DF, hoje, tem mais de 3 milhões. Isso gera um imenso fluxo diário pendular entre o Plano Piloto e as cidades satélites", completa o presidente do CAU-DF.

Imagem aérea de Brasília mostra "tesourinhas" durante a construção da Capital Federal — Foto: Reprodução

Brasília é conhecida como cidade-parque -- parte do planejamento de Lúcio Costa para a construção da capital preservado até os dias atuais.

Segundo dados da Novacap, 65 mil das cerca de 79 mil árvores plantadas pela companhia urbanizadora entre 2024 e 2025 estão no centro da capital .

O mesmo não acontece em regiões periféricas: apenas 14 mil plantios foram em Samambaia , por exemplo, ainda de acordo com a Novacap.

'Racismo ambiental': foto comparando quantidade de árvores em duas regiões de Brasília viraliza nas redes sociais A justificativa para a diferença, segundo a companhia, é que o Plano Piloto tem áreas para arborização que foram planejadas e são preservadas. Já outras localidades tiveram "origem sem o devido planejamento ou critérios de preservação".

A relação entre a presença de áreas verdes e a mobilidade urbana pode não parecer óbvia, mas existe .

Segundo o professor de engenharia do UniCeub Rideci Farias, o uso intenso do concreto somado ao asfalto dos grandes eixos viários necessários para interligar as cidades contribui com o escoamento superficial: quando a água (das chuvas, por exemplo) é maior que a capacidade de infiltração do solo .

A consequência: inundações que impactam diretamente na mobilidade urbana – desde a oferta mais lenta de veículos, causado pelo trânsito, até falhas no fornecimento de energia que impactam o serviço do metrô, por exemplo.

"O Distrito Federal foi desenvolvido pensando muito na questão de mobilidade rodoviária. Apesar de algumas áreas terem certo planejamento, o DF não foi dimensionado para eventos extremos e mais frequentes e a gente tem uma fragilização do sistema", afirma o especialista.

articles.title: Ryan Blaney Has Black Eye, Talks Carson Hocevar Fight in New Video Ahead of Upcoming NASCAR Race
articles.summary: Ryan Blaney is sporting a black eye ahead of this weekend's Hollywood Casino 400 in Kansas City after what he described as an "uncharacteristic" altercation with Carson Hocevar last Saturday in Bristol.
articles.body:
Ryan Blaney is sporting a black eye ahead of this weekend's Hollywood Casino 400 in Kansas City after what he described as an "uncharacteristic" altercation with Carson Hocevar last Saturday in Bristol.

"It was definitely unlike me... it was kind of the opposite of how I normally am," Blaney told reporters Friday. "I get fired up quickly, but I calm down really quickly. The other night, it just kind of slowly built over the half hour or so."

Blaney also said his eye was fine but that he wished it had "healed a little bit quicker than this."

NASCAR Icon Has Progressive Brain Disease

The altercation between Blaney and Hocevar took place after Hocevar's No. 77 bumped Blaney's No. 12 Ford into the wall.

Blaney then approached Hocevar on pit road, where the two exchanged punches before being separated.

Blaney said Friday the confrontation was the result of a build-up of frustration over start to postseason marred by brake failure at Gateway and a failed pre-race technical inspection at Darlington.

"This Chase hasn't gone exactly how I thought it was gonna go. Just a couple of rough finishes, back to back... you start realizing, 'Man, it's going to be really hard to make up those points now,' and this is your season, this is what you're racing for," Blaney said. "So, I think all of those just kind of built."

About the inciting incident on the track, Blaney said he thought on review the contact had been "pretty 50/50."

"I thought, just kind of a racing thing of Bristol, of two guys being aggressive with the line they wanted to be in," Blaney said.

Hocevar also seemed to be over the fight ahead of this weekend's action at Kansas Speedway. He told reporters the incident made him "more of a fan" of Blaney.

The Chase continues Sunday with the fourth competition of the 10-race postseason at 3 p.m. ET at Kansas Speedway. Kyle Larson enters the race with a narrow lead over Denny Hamlin for pole position in the Cup Series standings .

articles.title: What Just Happened in NASCAR ARCA Kansas Race? Wild Crash Causes Chaos
articles.summary: What just happened in the NASCAR ARCA race at Kansas? Here’s what to know about the wild crash that caused chaos during the race. The post What Just Happened...
articles.body:
The Menards 150 remained under caution well past 9 p.m. ET Friday, with officials still sorting out the wreckage that swallowed championship leader Jake Bollman's Nitro Motorsports Toyota.

The crash scrambled the outlook for Bollman's ARCA Menards Series title fight with his own Nitro Motorsports teammate Thomas Annunziata.

Rain wiped out practice and qualifying earlier Friday, so ARCA lined up the field entirely by owner points, handing pole position to Gio Ruggiero's No. 18 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota and slotting Bollman's No. 20 Nitro Motorsports Toyota third.

Jake Bollman's Crash Sequence Comes Into Focus

The trouble started on lap 23, when Annunziata turned Bollman entering Turn 1. ARCA's official social media account posted video of that contact , a separate incident from the bigger wreck that followed. Bollman's Nitro Motorsports Toyota absorbed only cosmetic damage and pressed on.

The far more serious crash arrived near the race's midpoint, when Bollman's No. 20 made contact with a spinning Will Kimmel's No. 69 Kimmel Racing Ford. Bollman then came to a stop near the top of the track before Austin Vaughn's No. 91 Maples Motorsports Ford T-boned him, according to NASCAR insider Bob Pockrass's account of the wreck .

Bollman climbed out of the car under his own power, and no injuries have been reported for him or any other driver caught up in the incident. Earlier reports also placed Michael Maples' car in the mix, though the clearest accounts center on the Kimmel and Vaughn contact.

Minutes after climbing out, Bollman found an FS1 interviewer and delivered a defiant message.

"Let's go out there and get this championship back," he said, according to motorsports reporter Joseph Srigley .

He acknowledged the wreck could hurt his championship push, but said that setbacks are part of who he is and that he'll bounce back, even if the turnaround doesn't come the same night.

"We're gonna get it back out there because we're never giving up," Bollman told TV cameras .

Bollman's No. 20 crew went to work on the mangled Toyota rather than parking it for the night, aiming to get their driver back on the track and salvage whatever points remain available, according to pit-lane reporting .

Bollman entered Friday having finished outside the top 10 only once all season, an 18th-place run at Talladega Superspeedway, according to a Racing America guide .

That consistency now hangs on the outcome of a bent-up race car. Should Bollman wind up last in the 27-car field, Annunziata would need only an 11th-place finish or better to steal the championship away, according to unofficial scenarios .

Should the two Nitro Motorsports teammates finish the season deadlocked in points, Annunziata already holds the tiebreaker from his win earlier this year at Lime Rock Park, according to Speedway Digest .

The race resumed with FS1's broadcast continuing as crews worked to get cars, including Bollman's No. 20, ready to resume.

articles.title: Williams devuelve la fe a Carlos Sainz
articles.standfirst: El español firmó en Bakú su primera Q3 de la temporada (9º puesto) y la realidad competitiva del FW48 cambia gracias a las mejoras. Saldrá 14º por sanción
articles.summary: El español firmó en Bakú su primera Q3 de la temporada (9º puesto) y la realidad competitiva del FW48 cambia gracias a las mejoras. Saldrá 14º por sanción
articles.body: Un grito resumía todo con sencillez: "¡Vamos!". Era de Carlos Sainz, que 12 meses después volvía a sonreír en Bakú, una pista en la que sólo tiene ese brillante podio de 2025 pero casi que sirve como medicina a los males. Porque su Williams, que navegaba entre el sobrepeso desde el mes de enero y una carga aerodinámica deficiente, no invitaba al optimismo. Cada vez más desesperante y difícil. Hasta que llegó la mejora del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán y como un disparo entró en Q3. No son los podios ni lo que Sainz quería, pero ya es algo a lo que agarrarse. Porque su coche elevó la competitividad. Pasó de sólo pelearse con Cadillac o Aston Martin a tutear a los Alpine y dejar atrás a Audi, Haas y RB. Puede que no signifique un gran botín de puntos, pero ya es un coche diferente, que en Grove ha sido creado para enmendar la serie de errores gravísimos. "Ha sido un año muy complicado y es difícil cuando el invierno no va como quieres y cometes errores. Pero el trabajo que hicimos... es el mismo que hace un equipo que lucha por todo", explicaba el padre del proyecto, James Vowles, en DAZN. El coche vive, por lo menos, y ya tiene algo sobre lo que apoyar al pilotaje de Sainz. "Trajimos cambios en la aerodinámica, un nuevo chasis... Es la recompensa a un año con muchas noches sin dormir. Aquí [en Bakú] vamos bien, pero probaremos el chasis en Singapur y Malasia", apuntó Vowles. Es optimista, pero cauto. Algo lógico, aunque lo importante es que en su fábrica ya hay un trabajo que ha funcionado y es algo que perseguían. También hay más cosas, entre bastidores, que les hace creer que el futuro será mejor. Pero primero va el presente y Sainz puede volver a pelear por algunos puntos. "No siempre pelearemos en la Q3. El coche es mejor, aunque los Alpine, por ejemplo, van rápido. Pero podremos pelear por los puntos", contó Vowles en relación a Azerbaiyán. Que 12 meses después puede ayudar a cambiar dinámicas. De hecho, es como otra oportunidad en la mesa de Sainz. En 2025 había un gran coche y el español subió al podio para hacer ver que su cambio desde Ferrari no era tan negativo. En 2026, el 55 trasladó toda la confianza al proyecto con la renovación y ya ve que hay un salto que hace un puñado de carreras parecía lejano. "Llevo conduciendo bien todo el año, pero no había podido brillar el resultado. Hacía vueltas parecidas, pero salía el 16", repetía el español. La cosa ahora cambia. No significa que puedan tutear a Mercedes o Ferrari como ocurría en 2025 y probablemente en circuitos de diferente tipología vuelvan a sufrir. Pero ya hay un punto positivo en una campaña que debía haber enseñado un coche como el de Bakú unas carreras antes. Todo empezó a contrapié. Y el cambio llega tarde. Pero llega. "Estoy muy feliz por el puesto en parrilla porque quería devolver, un poco, todos esos esfuerzos a la fábrica en el nuevo chasis y la mejora de suelo que tenemos. Intentamos salir del hoyo y esto nos ayudará a impulsar nuestra moral", cerró el 55. Ya tiene motivos para la fe.

articles.title: Formula 1: Jamie Chadwick says testing F1 car is 'highlight' of career
articles.summary: Jamie Chadwick says testing a Formula 1 car is the highlight of her motorsport career.
articles.body:
One of the world's most decorated female racing drivers, Jamie Chadwick has described testing a Formula 1 car as the highlight of her motorsport career.

Britain's Chadwick joins an exclusive list of women to have driven an F1 car, after taking part in 32 laps at the Portimao circuit in Portugal, which will be on the F1 calendar in 2027.

The 28-year-old first joined Formula 1 team Williams in 2019 as a development driver and has gone on to win all three seasons of the all-female W Series, as well as being the first female driver to win a road race in IndyCar's feeder series.

She told BBC Sport: "In terms of a dream or a bucket list item, it's definitely the top.

"It was pretty surreal. It's kind of everything I imagined, but more. The feeling you get from a car like that is pretty incredible. And then at a track like Portimao, it's a proper rollercoaster."

She practised in a simulator beforehand and took part in a detailed programme of gym work, which included neck strengthening sessions, with some of the drivers on the F1 grid.

"I train my neck anyway for what I do, but it's that times 10. Just the sheer level of strength that's required in the neck is huge," she said.

"I can't really put it into words the G-force and the feeling on your neck. As soon as you accelerate out of the pit-lane, your head hits the back of the headrest because it's so aggressive.

"You wake up the next morning like you've been in a fight with Mike Tyson. It feels like you've been beaten about a bit, but it's an incredible feeling."

There are now 13 women who have driven an F1 car. Five of those have officially entered a F1 Grand Prix weekend, and only two have gone on to actually take part in a race.

50 years and counting since last female F1 driver

Maria Teresa de Filippis made history as the first female in 1958 when she took part in the Belgium Grand Prix, finishing 10th.

It took 15 years to see the next woman in an F1 car. The legendary Lella Lombardi took part in a record 17 grands prix, including the Spanish GP in 1975, where she finished sixth, becoming the first and so far only woman to score points.

In 2014, Susie Wolff made the first female appearance in an official F1 session for more than two decades, when she drove a Williams car at the British Grand Prix.

Wolff, who is now the managing director of the all-female series F1 Academy, has been instrumental in helping more females get into the sport and was one of the "inspirations" behind Chadwick wanting to drive an F1 car.

Chadwick is not the only woman to have driven an F1 car this year. Doriane Pin, who won the F1 Academy title in 2025, became the first female to drive a Mercedes in April.

But despite the progress, no woman has started an F1 race since Lombardi, 50 years ago.

Chadwick believed that women are "capable of competing in Formula 1", but that there "shouldn't be a timeline on it".

"I definitely believe the talent is out there," she said, adding: "And I'm excited.

"Me doing this test and Williams giving opportunities to female drivers for example, will hopefully lead to a race seat one day."

But with only 22 seats in F1, it is extremely tough for any driver to break into.

Chadwick said: "You're looking at F2, F3 champions not getting seats and you realise that there's more talent than there are seats often available. Then you narrow it down to a female driver and it's even tougher and an even smaller talent pool.

"But I genuinely believe with everything that we're doing now to support female talent it's only going to lead in a positive direction."

articles.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Eye Of Dubai looks to retain Ripon crown
articles.summary: Eye Of Dubai goes for a third successive triumph in Ripon's Cathedral City Of The Dales Handicap - live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday afternoon; Later on, El Cordobes and Pride Of Arras headline the Joe Hirsch Stakes
articles.body:
3.28 Ripon - Eye Of Dubai bids for a third win in the race

Eye Of Dubai seeks a third consecutive success in the feature Ripon Cathedral City Of The Dales Handicap .

John and Sean Quinn's five-year-old returned to winning ways when claiming the Ayr Bronze Cup last weekend and this course specialist must be feared from this 5lb higher mark.

Stalemate Dark Thirty is a noteworthy runner after his excellent third at the Curragh and the handicapper has given him a chance with a 2lb drop in the weights. Jake Dickson takes a further 5lb off, giving this gelded son of Starspangledbanner a real opportunity here.

Trefor is a course and distance winner who is closely matched with Indian Run on their Windsor 1-3 in August and both rate each-way contenders, despite the inconsistent recent efforts of the former.

David O'Meara saddles Yes I'm Mali who scored over this track and trip on his penultimate start and should go well with Conor Whiteley claiming a handy 5lb.

7.00 Southwell - Well-bred pair Pyramid and Kashooda headline

Pyramid and Kashooda contest a potentially informative Free Bets On attheraces.com Maiden Stakes at Southwell.

Juddmonte colt Pyramid caught the eye when runner-up at Wolverhampton on his debut in July, denied a run until the race was over, he stuck on nicely and should improve for that outing. The winner has since finished second in Listed company while the third scored next time so the form looks rock solid.

Kashooda is the main danger for Andrew Balding and Callum Hutchinson. She has placed on both starts to date including when second to a nice type at Kempton and ought to have more to offer.

Others to note include Roxy Power and Pepperazzi , who debuts in the Valmont silks for Oliver Cole.

10.19 Belmont Park - Pride Of Arras and El Cordobes lock horns

A cracking renewal of this Grade 1 Joe Hirsch Stakes sees European raiders El Cordobes and Pride Of Arras headline a field of seven.

Charlie Appleby's El Cordobes finished third behind stablemate Rebel's Romance in this race last year before producing a career best to claim the same spot in the Breeders' Cup Turf. Not seen since down the field in the H.H The Amir Trophy in February, he has claims if fit enough after this break.

Ralph Beckett's Pride Of Arras took the notable scalp of Gethin when landing the Group 3 September Stakes at Kempton and a similar display would give him an obvious chance as he heads up to Grade 1 company again.

Far Bridge took a Grade 3 on his last outing but was behind El Cordobes in this race last season, while the Ed Walker-trained Fort George has claims on the pick of his form.

The day begins with Grade 1 action from Australia, where Guest House and St Gotthard contest the Golden Rose Stakes at Rosehill (7.05am).

Back on home soil, Zarakova tops six runners in Ripon's 2.16pm Lloyd Landrover Ripon Nursery Handicap . In opposition is Palace Legacy , who steps into handicap company for the first time.

Auteuil's G3 Prix de Maisons-Laffitte at 2.50pm sees Leopard Du Berlais attempt to get back on track. The four-year-old won his first three starts by a combined 18 lengths but has failed to fire since. A market check could prove important.

Caragio was unlucky not to win the Leger Legends contest at Doncaster earlier this month, when trainer and owner Adam Kirby kicked for home slightly early aboard this son of Caravaggio. Down 1lb for that effort, he will be well-fancied in Southwell's 8pm At The Races App Expert Tips Handicap .

Stateside, Sunlit Uplands , Esna , Cathedral and Kathynmarissa all line up for the G2 Flower Bowl at Belmont before Santa Anita plays host to the Goodwood Stakes at 12.30am.

articles.title: ‘No one will marry her’: Baranica Elangovan defies village taunts to make pole vault history at Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Baranica Elangovan, the Asian Games bronze medal in Nagoya was about much more than clearing a bar at 4.15m.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Baranica Elangovan, the Asian Games bronze medal in Nagoya was about much more than clearing a bar at 4.15m. It was a moment of vindication after years of injury, doubt and questions over whether a woman from her village should even be taking up a sport considered risky.When the 24-year-old Indian took up pole vaulting, people around her questioned the decision and warned her parents that an injury could affect her future.“I come from a village. When I started, I underwent ACL surgery after an injury while vaulting in 2019. At that time, everyone was telling my parents, ‘Why let a girl take part in Pole Vault? This event is quite risky. If something happens to her, no one will marry her.’ They were talking behind our backs,” Elangovan told IANS after winning bronze.But her parents refused to listen.“But my mum and dad believed in me. They spoke clearly with the coach, and my coach believed in my talent. He told them, ‘She’ll be able to do more than you think. She’ll definitely shine in sport.’ They believed him, and I want to thank them too, because they didn’t listen to others; they believed in me,” she said.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleFrom ACL surgery to Asian Games historyElangovan's journey to the podium was hardly conventional. After moving from Mayiladuthurai to Chennai for college, she initially pursued long jump and triple jump before unexpectedly finding her way into pole vault.“I was part of the triple jump. I was searching for a coach for the triple jump, but unexpectedly, I got a coach for the pole vault because of the event. After seeing the event, I got really excited, and I just wanna give it a try. That's how I entered the pole vault. After entering the sport, I started to follow the routines and everything,” she said.Five years after undergoing ACL surgery, Elangovan cleared 4.15m in Nagoya to become the first Indian to win an Asian Games medal in pole vault. She finished tied with Kazakhstan's Polina Ivanova, with the bronze eventually decided on countback after both athletes failed at 4.25m.Even then, Elangovan did not immediately realise she had made history.“I didn’t believe I’d won the medal. My colleague came up and said, ‘You were at the bronze, you won it.’ There was another athlete sharing the bronze, the Kazakhstan athlete. My colleague told me that I was tied at third for the Bronze medal. Only after that did I find out. I was aiming for a PB (Personal Best), but I actually got the medal.”Her focus throughout the competition had been performance rather than the podium.“I was not aiming for the medal, actually. I was aiming for the performance. I just wanted to hit my PB [Personal Best] today. That's the one thing on my mind: running. I need to do. I need to do. I need to do. I was really aggressive with my pole and run-up...,” she said.‘This is for you, Anna’Elangovan also credited the Athletics Federation of India for ensuring that her pole reached Japan and for arranging a preparatory camp that helped her adapt to the conditions.“This time, our Athletics Federation of India tried every possible way with every airline to take our poles, and they made it really possible. I also want to thank the Athletics Federation of India. It was only because of them that I could win this medal,” she said.“There was a preparatory camp at Sugupa University one week before the Asian Games, which helped me adapt to the environment, timings, food and recovery. They sorted everything out for us, and it was really nice,” she added.After overcoming the doubts that accompanied her journey, Elangovan knew exactly who she wanted to dedicate the medal to.“I’m dedicating this to my coach, Milber Bertrand Russell.”“This is for you, Anna,” she said while dedicating the medal to Russell.And she hopes her medal will change perceptions around the event she once entered almost by chance.“Definitely! When I started, there were only five to six competitors. Now, you can see around 15 competitors, and many more young athletes are doing it in the under-20 category. I can see it, and definitely, India will be able to see a change in pole vault history, with the performance also,” she said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Antonelli debería llegar a liderar unas vueltas antes que en Monza"
articles.standfirst: Russell, irónico, no descarta a Kimi como posible candidato al triunfo pese a que sale desde el 16º
articles.summary: Russell, irónico, no descarta a Kimi como posible candidato al triunfo pese a que sale desde el 16º
articles.body: En Monza, Antonelli salía 18º por una penalización de cambio de motor y hoy lo hará desde el 16º, tras un error de pilotaje en el que destrozó la suspensión de su Mercedes en la Q1 en Baku. Sin embargo, George Russell, el 'poleman' no descarta a su compañero como posible candidato a la victoria, a pesar de que el italiano no ha estado fluido en todo el fin de semana respecto a su ritmo y tendrá coches muy complicados de superar en el camino. "Obviamente, no se puede descartar a Kimi. Empezó en la 19ª posición en Monza y ahora está en la 16ª, así que debería liderar algunas vueltas antes esta vez", dijo de forma irónica Russell y aludiendo a que en Monza, con una estratagia cambiada de salir con suros, Antonelli llegó al primero en sólo 18 vueltas. "Él [Antonelli] ha estado impecable durante toda la temporada. Creo que si analizas cualquier campaña de campeonato, incluso la de los ganadores, siempre hay errores por el camino. Así que sigo creyendo y sigo luchando hasta que ya no sea posible. Pero no siento ninguna presión. Siento emoción cada vez que me subo al coche ahora, simplemente porque me siento más seguro en mí mismo", decía sobre los 81 puntos que le separan en el Mundial de su compañero. "Cuando empiezas a ganar confianza, se genera un ciclo ascendente. Por otro lado, cuando estás en desventaja, empiezas a perder esa confianza, y entonces empiezas a forzar más los límites, y es entonces cuando se cometen errores. Pero, como ya dije, él ha estado impecable esta temporada. Es el primer error que comete en una clasificación o carrera en todo el año", subrayaba. Además, Russell cree que Verstappen "podría ser un rival por la victoria también". Max sufrió un problema de motor (entrega eléctrica) en la qualy y parte octavo, pero visto su ritmo todo el fin de semana puede que se meta en la pelea. Eso sí, nadie ha logrado una pole tan holgada en todo el año como los 0.837 segundos que el británico el endosó ayer a Leclerc.

articles.title: Carrera F1 del GP de Azerbaiyán en directo | Alonso y Sainz en Bakú hoy en vivo
articles.summary: ¡HAMILTON PASA A NORRIS! El de McLaren parece tener varios problemas. De Russell ni nos preocupamos. El británico tiene un ritmazo, rodando en 1.47, s
articles.body:
Última hora del GP Azerbaiyán en directo:

La carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán se presenta como una prueba de fuego para un Mundial que parece inclinarse cada vez más a favor de Andrea Kimi Antonelli .

El joven piloto italiano se postula como claro favorito a llevarse el título ante unos rivales que cada vez lo dan más por perdido. Sin embargo, este fin de semana, se han girado las tornas. El líder del Mundial partirá 16º en carrera , debido a un error cometido durante la Q1, al chocar con el muro y romper la suspensión de su monoplaza, impidiéndole participar en Q2 y marcar un mejor tiempo para luchar por la Pole. Una Pole que se llevó, sin embargo, su compañero de equipo, Geroge Russell . El británico ha mostrado bastante superioridad durante el fin de semana al llevarse el Libre 1 y el Libre 2, marcando un tiempo finalmente de 1.42.526 y llevándose de tal forma la Pole en Bakú.

Al Poleman le siguen Leclerc y Piastri , a más de 8 décimas. Ambos pilotos parecían estar tapados durante el fin de semana, pero finalmente pudieron hacer una gran vuelta para posicionarse en las primeras líneas de parrilla. Por el contrario, Max Verstappen, parecía ser el único capaz de tumbar a los Mercedes al batallarles los tiempos durante todos los entrenamientos, e incluso llevarse el Libre 3. Sin embargo, el neerlandés se quedó a segundo y medio del británico y tendrá que partir 8º, por detrás Gasly .

Mientras, los españoles fueron la cara y la cruz de la clasificación . Por un lado, Fernando Alonso sigue teniendo bastantes problemas con su Aston Martin y, en especial, con el motor Honda. Llegaba con una penalización de 25 posiciones , es decir, saldrá último, al cambiar su motor. No obstante, dicho motor nuevo sufrió una fuga de aceite, teniendo que regresar al motor antiguo y conservando, aún y así, la penalización.

Por otro lado, Carlos Sainz pudo sacar provecho de las mejoras del Williams y, no sólo al meterse en Q3 , sino que además pudo clasificar 9º en parrilla . No obstante, una sanción impuesta por la FIA al no respetar una bandera amarilla durante la Q3, baja al madrileño a la 14ª posición , limitando así mucho las opciones de Sainz a entrar en los puntos.

articles.title: F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting grid, news, live updates: George Russell clinches pole position after Kimi Antonelli crashes out in qualifying
articles.summary: F1 heads back to the Baku City Circuit for the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body: Formula 1 is heading back to the Baku City Circuit on Saturday for the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The grid is officially set, with Mercedes' George Russell clinching his fifth pole position of the season with a qualifying time of 1:42.526, edging out second-place Charles Leclerc by 0.837 seconds. Two of his wins came from the pole this year, including the Australian and Austrian GP, and he'll look to make it a third on Saturday morning.Kimi Antonelli, currently leading the F1 standings with 292 points (8 wins, 12 podiums), is racing from the 16th spot after crashing out in Q1, leaving his teammate, Russell, with the opportunity to make up some ground. Will Antonelli's qualifying crash out pave the way for Russell to make up some ground in the standings?
